Chapter 7: Faith—Trusting Beyond What Can Be Seen.
Imagine standing right at the edge of a dark forest. You can’t see what’s ahead. The path sort of disappears into the shadows, and you have no idea what waits on the other side. What would you do? Some people freeze, waiting for a sign or some proof before they take that first step. Others, though, decide to move forward—trusting that, even if they can’t see every detail, the ground beneath them will hold.
That’s the kind of faith we’re talking about here. It’s not blind optimism or just hoping for the best. Think about the trust a child has in a parent’s promise—even if they can’t picture exactly how things will work out. Faith is a choice to lean on something, or someone, beyond yourself, especially when those nagging doubts and fears start to creep in.
For a lot of people, faith starts with a moment of conviction—a flash of clarity when something just feels undeniably true. But here’s the real challenge: what happens when that feeling fades, or when life gets tough? It’s pretty easy to have faith when everything’s going your way. But when the road gets rocky, faith turns from a feeling into a choice.
Let me share a story. There was someone who went through a season when everything seemed to unravel—a job was lost, a relationship ended, and suddenly, they were left with a deep sense of failure. In that darkness, all the old certainties seemed to disappear. But instead of giving up, they decided to trust that there was still a purpose, even if they couldn’t see it yet. The days felt long, and answers didn’t come quickly. Looking back, though, they realized that time shaped them in ways they never expected—it made them more compassionate, and a whole lot more resilient.
So, faith isn’t about ignoring reality, or pretending pain doesn’t exist. It’s about holding on, even when you have no idea how things will turn out. It’s that quiet confidence that there’s meaning in the struggle, and that your story isn’t finished yet.
Most people don’t realize this, but faith actually grows stronger the more it’s tested. Every single time you choose to trust, even if you’re filled with doubt, your roots go a bit deeper. It’s usually not dramatic. It’s more like the steady, almost invisible growth of a tree—slow, but so strong when the storms finally come.
And here’s something else to remember: faith means letting go of the urge to control everything. It’s about being willing to accept help, admit weakness, and rely on grace. That can feel scary—maybe even impossible. But time and again, people who take that leap find something unexpected. There’s a freedom that comes with letting go—a release from anxiety, and a peace that doesn’t depend on your circumstances.
